newsitem.title: CHINA: Property stocks drag down HK market.
newsitem.headline: Property stocks drag down HK market.

text.p: Property stocks pulled down the Hong Kong market again on Friday morning and prices were expected to undergo more volatility in the short term, analysts and brokers said.
"This is just a storm in a teacup," said Andrew Taylor, property analyst at Asia Equity. "But we will continue to see volatility until we see some primary property (market) sales."

All blue chip property counters were down in late morning trade and the property sub-index was off 2.67 percent to 23,525, compared with the blue-chip Hang Seng Index's fall of 1.22 percent to 14,872.
"I've heard nothing new. This is just the general negative sentiment surrounding Tung's comments," said Chris Geiger, associate director at Vickers Ballas.
"It is way overdone," he added. "Tung is not going to wreck the market."
Hong Kong's new Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa said before and after he took up his post on Tuesday that he will increase the supply of land and the number of public housing units completed each year.
But Tung has yet to reveal details of his housing plan and this had unsettled the market, brokers said.
Property counters have a weighting of about 30 percent on the blue-chip index.
Sun Hung Kai Properties led the sector down again, falling HK$3.50 to HK$85.25.
Cheung Kong slipped HK$2.50 to HK$71.25 and New World Development dropped HK$1.20 to HK$45.30.
Henderson Land lost HK$1.75 to HK$64.00 and Sino Land fell HK$0.45 to HK$7.75.
Hang Lung Development eased HK$0.20 to HK$14.10.
